next.reason: The catalog rule carries the whole 1985 class-condition text: the class-name-1 test, the format, 'The usage of the operand being tested must be described as DISPLAY', NOT, the NUMERIC/ALPHABETIC/ALPHABETIC-LOWER/-UPPER tests and their bans, valid signs, and 'The class-name-1 test must not be used with an item whose data description describes the item as numeric' (§1985:VI.6.3.1.2). The tests themselves are kept (§2023:8.8.4.4.4 GR3 f) 'the condition is true if the content ... consists entirely of the characters listed in the definition of class-name-1', n) for NUMERIC, signs per §2023:13.18.52.4 GR5 and GR6; NOT per §2023:8.8.4.4.4 GR2 'the truth value is reversed'; format §2023:8.8.4.4.2). The operand rules differ both ways: §2023:8.8.4.4.3 SR8 lets NUMERIC test a numeric item of any usage and an alphabetic item or a group with signed subordinates, all refused in 1985; §2023:8.8.4.4.3 SR4 newly refuses ALPHABETIC, ALPHABETIC-LOWER, ALPHABETIC-UPPER or class-name-1 on a numeric-edited item, which 1985 allowed (it barred only numeric items); §2023:8.8.4.4.3 SR3 admits national usage. A valid 1985 program such as 'IF EDITED-ITEM IS ALPHABETIC' is refused in 2023.
